name: Train Street
kicker: The railway lane between Le Duan and Phung Hung
summary: A working railway runs through a residential lane between Le Duan and Phung Hung, with house fronts, plants, and cafe stools a step from the rails. Tour groups have been asked to stay away since March 2025. If you go, go on your own, stay off the tracks, and watch from the side.
getThere: Walk from the lake. Stay off the rails.
heroCaption: A train in the lane at Train Street
gettingThere: Walk from Hoan Kiem to the Tran Phu–Phung Hung section of the line. The full corridor runs about 2 km from Le Duan to Phung Hung.
hours: Check on arrival. No visitor timetable or cafe price published.
closed: Department of Tourism asked agencies not to run tours in Cua Nam, Hang Bong, and Cua Dong wards (March 2025). VnExpress: officially closed in September 2022. Neither report bars individuals from watching off the rails.

links.label: VietnamPlus, 10 March 2025
links.note: The department asked agencies not to run tours.

notice.title: Tours have been asked to stop
notice.body: In March 2025 Hanoi's Department of Tourism asked agencies not to run tours here. Do not stand on the tracks.

body: The tracks squeeze between house fronts, potted plants, and cafe stools along a corridor of about 2 km, from Le Duan through Tran Phu and Cua Dong to Phung Hung. The Tran Phu to Phung Hung section is about 300 m.

Between trains it is a residential lane, and visitors have no timetable to plan around, so do not build a day on catching a train. Keep it short, stay off the rails, and leave the lane to the people who live there.

figures.caption: The lane in daylight, between trains
figures.alt: A railway track running between house fronts and cafe signs in Hanoi's Train Street

legs.heading: From Hoan Kiem
legs.body: Walk to Tran Phu or Phung Hung.
